subject.title: [Feature]: Plugin API for aborting agent runs (api.runtime.agent.abort)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a supported plugin runtime abort API, and if so what ownership, session, and permission boundary must it enforce?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but granting plugin code authority to abort arbitrary run ids is a product and security-boundary choice that automation cannot safely infer.

options.title: Design a scoped plugin abort API
options.body: Approve a narrow `api.runtime.agent.abort` contract only after defining session/run ownership checks, trusted-plugin access, docs, and focused Gateway/plugin runtime tests.

options.title: Use existing Gateway cancellation only
options.body: Decline a new runtime method and document `chat.abort` or session cancellation as the supported path for trusted in-process plugins or operator clients.

options.title: Defer for broader lifecycle design
options.body: Keep this open but block implementation until plugin lifecycle permissions and run-management APIs are designed together.

recommendation.title: Design a scoped plugin abort API
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow `api.runtime.agent.abort` contract only after defining session/run ownership checks, trusted-plugin access, docs, and focused Gateway/plugin runtime tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a Plugin SDK/Gateway product and security-boundary decision, and this handle is the strongest available routing candidate from adjacent runtime history and prior review context.
